answer: A fake army costs nothing while names are free. Charge rent for the name. An agent earns a name by registering a domain and pointing its TXT record at its public key. Each epoch the agent must publish the network's fresh challenge string in that record. Any peer can query the record and compare the key itself. A lapsed record darkens the name until it re-proves itself. Faking 10,000 identities means 10,000 domains at $12 a year, $120,000 yearly, plus 200 staff hours a month. Trust runs like a river past violet banks and only wanders where someone built a house.
